newsitem.title: UK: BOE's George says aims to pre-empt inflation.
newsitem.headline: BOE's George says aims to pre-empt inflation.

text.p: The short term outlook for inflation is encouraging but the Bank of England is more concerned about containing inflationary pressures that may be building up in the longer term, central bank Governor Eddie George said.
"That's what we're about, pre-emptive action to moderate the pace of the upswing to a sustainable pace rather than leave it too little, too late," Geworge said on BBC radio 4.
George said he was optimistic about the state of inflation now but remained concerned about the impact of the current strong economic growth.
"At the moment in the short run, it's extremely encouraging, there are very, very few inflationary pressures to be seen anywhere in the system, that's not been our concern," he said.
"What we're also seeing is robust domestic demand growth at a rate which can't be sustained for very long without actualy that giving rise to inflationary pressures further down the track.
That's essentially the concern not this year but next year and into 1999."
